metadata.title: Assembled blocks — standard-enablement
metadata.audience: Customer champions and engineers in a Cursor demo

slides.headline: Standard enablement spine — assembled for review

content.subtitle: Prove Rules stay on with Lab 4 · Encode brand once so Agents and exporters share tokens · Catch thin decks with /deck-score before export · Run the same Agent from the terminal with Cursor CLI · Spend context on the task, not on rule bloat · Answer privacy questions and show how review gates work

notes.opening: Candidate standard deck — leave-behind plus curriculum drafts.
points: Edit blocks under content-blocks/, then re-run assemble.
CLI / tokens / privacy stay draft until SME sign-off.

slides.headline: Prove the three primitives in twenty minutes

notes.opening: We pause the feature tour here on purpose.
points: The PPTX already proved the pipeline works.
These labs make Rules, Skills, and Agents feel different.
Exit criteria beat another slide walkthrough.
notes.transition: Start with Rules — the always-on layer.

slides.headline: Rules shape every Agent reply without typing slash

bullets.text: Always-on brand rule loads in every chat
bullets.detail: .cursor/rules/<slug>-brand.mdc with alwaysApply: true

bullets.text: Workflow rule loads when you work on decks
bullets.detail: deck-workflow.mdc — process, not brand voice

bullets.text: Ask for a topic-label headline and watch the rewrite
bullets.detail: Insight headlines and banned phrases come from the rule

content.takeaway: If it should always apply, it is a Rule — not a Skill.

notes.opening: Open the brand rule and point at alwaysApply.
points: Contrast brand rule with deck-workflow.
Live ask: write a content slide titled Q2 Results.
Call out the insight rewrite without pasting the rule.
notes.transition: Skills are what people choose to run.

slides.headline: Skills are the buttons; agents are the pipeline

bullets.text: Humans type slash commands under /
bullets.detail: create-brief, write-slide, brand-check, export-pptx, build-deck

bullets.text: Atomic skills beat a full rebuild for small edits
bullets.detail: /write-slide then /export-pptx — no /build-deck required

bullets.text: brand-check wraps brand-guardian
bullets.detail: Customers rarely type agent names; skills choose when

content.takeaway: Teach the button first; the pipeline is why it scales.

notes.opening: Open the slash menu and find the deck skills.
points: Run write-slide only on one headline.
Export PPTX to show the atomic path.
Open brand-check and name the agent behind it.

slides.headline: Lab 4 catches the bad edit you introduce on purpose

bullets.text: Break one headline or insert a banned phrase
bullets.detail: Topic label like Overview, or a phrase from brand/voice.md

bullets.text: Run /brand-check and expect warn or fail
bullets.detail: Optional: delete a takeaway and run /deck-score

bullets.text: Fix, then /export-pptx
bullets.detail: Pass when brand-guardian flags the deliberate violation

content.takeaway: Quality is enforced in the repo — not by hoping presenters remember.

notes.opening: This is the required exit for the leave-behind demo.
points: Have someone else introduce the break if the room is large.
Show the flag, then the fix.
Point at docs/primitives-lab.md for the full twenty minutes.
notes.transition: Next block: where brand tokens live so Agents and exporters agree.

slides.headline: Encode brand once — Agents and exporters share it

notes.opening: This is the Encode brand teachable moment.
points: Studio writes rules and brand assets, not a finished customer deck.
Same tokens show up in Cursor and in Office exporters.
notes.transition: Start with what lands in the zip.

slides.headline: One pack feeds always-on rules and the exporters

bullets.text: Colors, fonts, and voice become an always-on rule
bullets.detail: .cursor/rules/<slug>-brand.mdc shapes Agent output in every chat

bullets.text: brand/ mirrors the same tokens for humans and exporters
bullets.detail: brand-pack.json, palette, voice, logos on dark and light

bullets.text: Layout style sets slide mix and frame treatment
bullets.detail: classic, minimal, or bold — Agents and PPTX stay aligned

content.takeaway: Encode once in Studio; regenerate the zip when brand changes.

notes.opening: Walk the Encode brand fields without drowning in hex.
points: Call out logos on dark vs light.
Mention words-to-avoid as brand-guardian fuel.
Preview shows the layout style before download.
notes.transition: Same factory, more than one Office renderer.

slides.headline: PPTX is the proof; Doc and workbook reuse the tokens

bullets.text: Happy path stays /create-brief → /build-deck → PPTX
bullets.detail: output/ appears after skills run — not pre-built in the zip

bullets.text: Optional /build-doc and /export-metrics-xlsx
bullets.detail: Thin skills; same brand tokens; not a design-agency replacement

bullets.text: Day 2: brand stays owned by marketing plus champion
bullets.detail: See docs/after-the-demo.md for regenerate vs edit

content.takeaway: Renderers are skills; the product is the Cursor factory.

notes.opening: Toggle factory outputs in Studio if you are mid-demo.
points: Keep silhouettes honest — Doc/XLSX are not finished files in Studio.
Point champions at after-the-demo ownership table.
notes.transition: Next: catch thin decks before export.

slides.headline: Gate quality before the PPTX leaves the room

notes.opening: Two gates, one leave-behind.
points: brand-check is the judgment call.
deck-score is the structural CLI.

slides.headline: Judgment and structure catch different failures

content.takeaway: Run both before you call the demo done.

notes.opening: Do not collapse these into one button in the story.
points: Champions can wire smoke:deck-quality into CI later.
Studio UI for scores is intentionally out of scope.
notes.transition: Lab 4 optional path makes the CLI real.

slides.headline: Delete a takeaway and watch /deck-score move

bullets.text: Strip depth from one slide on purpose
bullets.detail: Remove takeaway or flatten assertion+detail bullets

bullets.text: Run /deck-score before you fix it
bullets.detail: Optional --strict if the champion wants a hard gate

bullets.text: Restore depth, re-score, then /export-pptx
bullets.detail: Pairs with the required /brand-check Lab 4 exit

content.takeaway: Thin decks fail in the repo — not in the customer meeting.

notes.opening: Only if Lab 4 already landed; otherwise demo the command on a sample.
points: Point at examples/delight-sample for a known baseline.
Mention docs/superpowers scorecard design for maintainers.

slides.headline: Run Agent from the terminal — same factory, more surfaces

notes.opening: This block is for engineers who will not live only in the IDE.
points: CLI is a first-class Agent surface, not a side tool.
Leave-behind Rules still apply when you run from the repo root.

slides.headline: Install once, then type agent in any project

bullets.text: Install from the official Cursor docs
bullets.detail: macOS/Linux: curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash · Windows: PowerShell irm install script

bullets.text: Authenticate and confirm who you are
bullets.detail: agent login · agent status · agent about

bullets.text: Start interactive Agent in the leave-behind repo
bullets.detail: cd into the zip · agent · or agent "explain the brand rule"

content.takeaway: The entrypoint to learn is agent — verify against cursor.com/docs/cli before you demo.

notes.opening: Do the install on a clean laptop once before the customer room.
points: If cursor alone errors, point them at agent as documented.
Stay in the leave-behind directory so Rules load.

slides.headline: Agent, Plan, and Ask work the same as in the IDE

bullets.text: Agent mode is the default — full tools for coding tasks
bullets.detail: No --mode flag required for the happy path

bullets.text: Plan before you build
bullets.detail: /plan, --plan, or --mode=plan — clarifying questions first

bullets.text: Ask stays read-only
bullets.detail: /ask or --mode=ask — explore without edits

content.takeaway: Teach one mode model: IDE and CLI share Agent / Plan / Ask.

notes.opening: Switch modes live with slash commands so muscle memory transfers.
points: Ask a Plan question about Lab 4 before any edit.
Remind them Rules and mcp.json are respected in CLI.

slides.headline: Print mode puts Agent into scripts and CI

bullets.text: Use -p / --print for non-interactive runs
bullets.detail: agent -p "review these changes for security issues" --output-format text

bullets.text: Hand off long work to Cloud Agent mid-session
bullets.detail: Prepend & to a message · pick up at cursor.com/agents

bullets.text: Resume and worktrees keep context under control
bullets.detail: agent resume · agent -w for an isolated git worktree

content.takeaway: CLI is how the factory shows up in automation — still rules-aware.

notes.opening: One print-mode demo is enough; do not boil the ocean on flags.
points: Sandbox: mention /sandbox if security folks are in the room.
Point reviewers at the draft status — SME should sanity-check before external share.
notes.transition: Close on when to use CLI vs IDE.

slides.headline: Pick the surface; keep the same Rules

bullets.text: IDE for live pairing and visual review
bullets.detail: Still the default for most ADM leave-behind demos

bullets.text: CLI for terminal-first engineers, scripts, and CI
bullets.detail: agent -p for print mode · same .cursor/rules in the repo

bullets.text: SME-review this block before external 101
bullets.detail: Draft status — verify flags at cursor.com/docs/cli/overview

content.takeaway: Surfaces differ; Rules travel with the repo.

notes.opening: Close on parity, not on memorizing every flag.
points: Docs source of truth: cursor.com/docs/cli/overview.
Next curriculum blocks: optimize-tokens, govern-privacy-and-review.

slides.headline: Context is a budget — spend it on the task

notes.opening: This is enablement priority two after CLI.
points: Not about shaving pennies — about quality of Agent answers.
Leave-behind brand rules are the good kind of always-on tax.

slides.headline: Always-on rules pay on every Agent turn

bullets.text: Applied rules are included at the start of model context
bullets.detail: Cursor Rules docs — persistent guidance, no memory between completions

bullets.text: alwaysApply: true means every chat pays the cost
bullets.detail: Use for brand voice and hard constraints — keep those files short

bullets.text: The leave-behind brand rule is intentional tax
bullets.detail: Do not delete it to “save tokens” — trim other always-on clutter instead

content.takeaway: Pay every turn only for what must always be true.

notes.opening: Open the brand .mdc and point at alwaysApply.
points: Contrast with deck-workflow — contextual, not always on.
Ask the room what they would wrongly put in alwaysApply.
notes.transition: Three other ways to apply rules.

slides.headline: Scope rules with globs, descriptions, or @ — not more always-on

bullets.text: Apply to Specific Files when a glob matches
bullets.detail: e.g. **/*.tsx patterns — see Cursor Rules glob table

bullets.text: Apply Intelligently when description is clear
bullets.detail: Agent decides from description — vague blurbs never load

bullets.text: Apply Manually for rare checklists
bullets.detail: @-mention the rule when you need it

content.takeaway: Same four modes as the docs — teach the dropdown, not a custom framework.

notes.opening: Draw the four-mode table on a whiteboard if helpful.
points: Good description reads like an API doc: what + when.
Point at primitives-decision-tree for Rule vs Skill vs Agent.
notes.transition: How to keep each rule file cheap.

slides.headline: Point at files — do not paste the whole guide into a rule

bullets.text: Keep rules focused; split large ones
bullets.detail: Official guidance: under 500 lines; composable .mdc files

bullets.text: Reference examples with @ instead of copying code
bullets.detail: Keeps rules short and stops them going stale

bullets.text: Skip what Agent and linters already know
bullets.detail: No full style guides in alwaysApply — encode only project-specific truth

content.takeaway: Short rules + pointers beat encyclopedias in context.

notes.opening: Show a bad fat rule vs a thin rule that @-references a template.
points: AGENTS.md is fine for simple cases — still keep it lean.
Team Rules exist on Team/Enterprise — mention, do not deep-dive.

slides.headline: New chat for a new job — stop attaching the whole repo

bullets.text: Start a fresh Agent chat when the task changes
bullets.detail: Long threads carry stale goals into the next request

bullets.text: Let Agent explore; attach only the files you know matter
bullets.detail: Prefer targeted @file over dumping a dozen paths

bullets.text: Index and ignore noise so search stays useful
bullets.detail: Keep generated junk out of the workspace the Agent walks

content.takeaway: Hygiene is a habit — Rules design plus session design.

notes.opening: This is the practical close for ADMs in the room.
points: Optional: show starting a new chat mid-demo after Lab 4.
SME should sanity-check before external 101.

slides.headline: Privacy for the vendor — review for the artifact

notes.opening: This is the content gap Gong/Granola kept surfacing in 101s.
points: Separate vendor privacy from leave-behind quality gates.
Stay on official docs — you are not legal counsel.

slides.headline: Privacy Mode: not used for training — with ZDR for most models

bullets.text: Privacy Mode: code is not used for training by Cursor or providers
bullets.detail: Stated in Cursor privacy help and data-use overview

bullets.text: Most models run under zero data retention agreements
bullets.detail: Providers do not store inputs/outputs for training under those agreements

bullets.text: Inference still sends prompts and code context to providers
bullets.detail: Do not claim the model runs fully offline — be precise

content.takeaway: Lead with Privacy Mode; never invent stronger guarantees than the docs.

notes.opening: Put the privacy URL on screen if you can.
points: Abuse/risk classifiers may retain data for investigation — mention if security is sophisticated.
Point to cursor.com/data-use for the canonical wording.

slides.headline: Enterprise turns Privacy Mode on by default — then enforce it

bullets.text: Enterprise: Privacy Mode on by default
bullets.detail: Teams/Enterprise admins can enforce org-wide from the dashboard

bullets.text: Block personal accounts on corporate devices when needed
bullets.detail: Allowed Team IDs / MDM — see Identity and Access Management docs

bullets.text: Enterprise extras exist for stricter programs
bullets.detail: CMEK, data residency, model access control — hand to account team

content.takeaway: Default plus enforce — do not rely on every developer finding a checkbox.

notes.opening: This is the slide GRC usually wants.
points: Do not deep-dive residency model lists unless asked.
Offer the enterprise privacy doc link as homework.

slides.headline: Be clear about Cloud Agents and retention-exception models

bullets.text: Cloud Agents store encrypted repo copies while they run
bullets.detail: Optional feature — if policy forbids storage, leave Cloud Agents off

bullets.text: Some models require provider retention and need admin opt-in
bullets.detail: Off by default under Privacy Mode until approved in the dashboard

bullets.text: BYOK and third-party gateways follow those providers’ policies
bullets.detail: US data residency docs explicitly exclude BYOK from residency guarantees

content.takeaway: Credibility comes from naming the exceptions before they do.

notes.opening: Security teams respect ADMs who volunteer the caveats.
points: IDE and CLI Agent without Cloud Agents still cover most leave-behind demos.
Re-check the models-with-retention section before each session.

slides.headline: Review the leave-behind before it leaves the room

bullets.text: /brand-check catches voice and insight failures
bullets.detail: brand-guardian — judgment gate from Lab 4

bullets.text: /deck-score catches thin structure
bullets.detail: CLI gate — warn by default, --strict when they want CI teeth

bullets.text: Same story in the IDE or with agent -p
bullets.detail: Governance of the artifact travels with the repo

content.takeaway: Vendor privacy + in-repo review — teach both in one breath.

notes.opening: Demo the Lab 4 break if you have not already.
points: Point at govern-quality-with-cli for the deeper scorecard story.
SME/security should sign off this block before external 101.

slides.headline: Next: SME sign-off, then Lab 4 in the room

items.action: Open the leave-behind zip in Cursor
Author new JTBD blocks under content-blocks/

notes.opening: Close on ownership and the required exit.
points: Mark reviewed blocks in catalog notes; re-assemble after edits.
Day-of kit: npm run field-kit · docs/adm-field-kit.md.
